The default qualitative palette

Source: R/colours.R
phw_default_palette.Rd

The palette that charts, tables and widgets use for groups when you don't name one. Out of the box it is "main" (navy, teal, orange, pink), carrying on into "extended" past four groups, so every chart in a report draws from one set of colours however many groups it has.

Usage

phw_default_palette()

Value

A palette name or vector.

Details

The colour-blind safe "accessible" palette is a switch you turn on once, and it then applies to every chart, table and widget, for any number of groups. The first of these that is set wins:

  1. options(phwstyle.palette = "accessible"), which is also what use_phw_ggplot(palette = "accessible") and the palette argument of phw_html_document(), phw_word_document() and phw_pdf_document() set.

  2. The environment variable PHWSTYLE_PALETTE, for switching one render from the command line without editing the document, e.g. PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible quarto render report.qmd.

  3. phw-palette: accessible in the YAML header of a Quarto or R Markdown document.

The option can also be any other palette name from phw_palettes, or your own vector of colours.

This switch changes colours only. Larger text and thicker lines are a separate setting, accessible = TRUE in theme_phw() or use_phw_ggplot(); neither turns the other on.

Examples

phw_default_palette()
#> [1] "main"
phw_pal(6)
#> [1] "#285087" "#24A2B5" "#FF5D0C" "#F43882" "#231F20" "#338276"

old <- options(phwstyle.palette = "accessible")
phw_pal(6)
#> [1] "#285087" "#24A2B5" "#FF5D0C" "#000000" "#9D5659" "#8478CF"
options(old)
